condition.purpose: Determine whether a 2-4 Unit property meets the STD-8.1 maximum CLTV.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report for property type and loan records for CLTV.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply the printed “Max CLTV: 80%” without a purpose split.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify property type and CLTV in the case record.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether CLTV is within the printed maximum.
checks: For a 2-4 Unit property, CLTV does not exceed 80%.

outcomes.criterion: The subject is a 2-4 Unit property and CLTV does not exceed 80%.
There is no case for this outcome.
The subject is a 2-4 Unit property and CLTV exceeds 80%.
The subject property is not a 2-4 Unit property.

rule.description: Apply the printed maximum CLTV for a 2-4 Unit property.

ledger.clause:
STD-8.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, Manufactured. Restrictions as printed: \[S: Subject Property Type\]

| **Property type** | **Purchase** | **Refi R/T** | **Refi C/O** | **Conditions as printed** |

| 2-4 Unit | 80% | 80% | 80% | Printed as “Max CLTV: 80%” with no purpose split |

STD-8.4 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” (STD-1.14). \[S: Subject Property Location\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a Condotel / PUDtel meets the applicable STD-8.1 limits and printed conditions.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report for property type and location, and review loan records for loan purpose and CLTV.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify the purchase, Refi R/T, or Refi C/O cap and the Florida condition printed in STD-8.1.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify CLTV, loan purpose, state, and minimum DSCR information.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable cap and conditions are met.

condition.purpose: Determine how the stated declining-market reduction applies to the property and borrower full profile and whether confirmation is needed for its combination with other caps.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report and other applicable property and borrower information for declining-market status.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile”.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Request Acra confirmation on how this reduction combines with other caps, as directed to Q-07.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the reduction and the confirmation result.
checks: For a declining market, “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” is applied.
Acra confirmation is obtained on how the reduction combines with other caps.

The property is in a declining market and Acra confirmation or information needed to apply the reduction remains outstanding.
The property is in a declining market and the stated reduction is not applied or the confirmed combined cap is not met.
The property is not in a declining market.

condition.purpose: Establish whether the property is considered listed for sale under STD-8.8.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review listing_history for the listing dates.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Measure from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify the listing lookback against the case record.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the property is considered listed for sale under §11.5.
checks: The property has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.

outcomes.criterion: The check holds; the property is considered listed for sale under §11.5.
There is no case for this outcome.
The check does not hold; the property is not considered listed for sale under §11.5.

rule.description: Determine whether the property meets the stated six-month listing lookback.

ledger.clause:
STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

clause_parts.text:
STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a property considered listed for sale meets the stated lien, occupancy, qualification, prepayment, reserves, amortization, LTV/CLTV, subordinate-financing, and impound requirements.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review listing_history, appraisal_report, credit and loan records, and documents establishing lien status, occupancy, prepayment penalty, reserves, subordinate financing, and impounds.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify each applicable STD-8.9 condition, including the lesser-of value basis for the 65% maximum LTV / CLTV.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify qualification by ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI, and verify the property's state for the prepayment-penalty exception.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether all applicable listed-property conditions are met.
checks: The property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
For investment properties, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
The loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI (Q-14).
A prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
Twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.
The loan has a fully amortizing term; interest only is not available.
Maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
No subordinate financing is allowed.
Impounds are required.

outcomes.criterion: The property is considered listed for sale and all applicable STD-8.9 conditions are met.
The property is considered listed for sale and a required document, information item, or determination remains outstanding.
The property is considered listed for sale and an applicable STD-8.9 condition is not met.
The property is not considered listed for sale under §11.5.

STD-1.10 Minimum loan amount \$100,000; maximum loan amount \$3,000,000; loan amount to be in \$50 increments. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.11 Seller concession / other contributions: limited to 3% of the sale price. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.12 Gifting is allowed and “requires borrower to contribute a minimum of 10% of the purchase price consisting of their own funds”; §8.7 states the contribution as the applicant's “own sourced and seasoned funds”. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section, not reproduced (Appendix B). \[S: Loan Amount; G §8.7, p. 12\]

STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve is met when the forbearance or mortgage-late trigger applies.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review credit_report, lease_agreement, rent_roll, and bank_statement for mortgage history, occupancy, rent receipt, and reserves.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether there was forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, the subject is tenant-occupied, and the prior two months' rent was not received timely.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If all stated trigger conditions apply, verify 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable reserve requirement is met, or whether the job does not apply.
checks: If there was forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, the subject is tenant-occupied, and the prior two months' rent was not received timely, 12 months of the subject's payment are in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.

ledger.clause:
STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

ledger.clause:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the entity has provided the required documentation without relying on borrower letters excusing missing documents.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Obtain and review the entity_documents, including formation documents and amendments, the applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws and amendments, ownership evidence, and all other documents required by STD-6.10.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the entity has provided the complete, legible documents applicable to its legal form, including the required ownership evidence and any applicable corporation or tax-year ownership evidence.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify name matching or a letter of explanation; the good-standing validity period; any required foreign qualification; the entity’s SS4, TIN, or EIN issuance letter or a submitted exception request; unanimous written consent or board resolution; and any required power of attorney. Do not accept a borrower letter stating required documents are not required, available, or excused.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether all applicable required documents and contents are present; refer any additional supporting-documentation condition to Legal as stated.
checks: A complete, legible Certificate of Formation or Articles of Organization and all amendments is provided.

For an LLC or Partnership, a complete, legible Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits and amendments is provided; for a corporation, complete, legible Bylaws with all referenced exhibits and amendments are provided.
The Operating Agreement or Bylaws states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.

All documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided; for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies or attaches all persons by name with their ownership interest, or membership interest certificates or units compliant with the Operating Agreement are provided.

For an S or C Corporation, compliant shareholder or stockholder certificates are provided, if any, or the stock ledger is provided if certificates are lost or unavailable; the certificate or ledger accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the formation documents, including those held by the corporation; and an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided if stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable.

For an S-corporation or Partnership where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest are provided; if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed, the letter includes a statement to that effect.
Names on the entity documents match the identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.

If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is conducted or where the property is located, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the applicable state is provided.

The entity’s IRS Form SS4, Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, or an EIN exception request is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

A Unanimous Written Consent or Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.
A Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee when required for that purpose.
A borrower letter is not used to state that required entity documents are not required, available, or excused.

ledger.clause:
6.2 Entity documentation
STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

6.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether title vesting in the trust meets the stated conditions.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the title commitment and the complete trust or Certification of Trust, together with any supporting documentation and written exception.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify the trust document contents, trust validity and revocability, trustors, beneficiaries, trustee powers, and any required written exception.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify the required provisions concerning title, mortgage authority, beneficiary consent, lender rights, and whether the trust has been revoked, modified, or amended; identify any additional documentation Legal requires.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether every applicable trust condition is met and whether any required written exception or conditioned supporting documentation remains outstanding.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust is provided, stating the Trust’s existence and date; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; whether the Trust is revocable and, if so, who holds the right to revoke; names and number of Trustees required to sign; Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.
The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.
The Trust is revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime; it is not irrevocable.
The Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.
The primary beneficiary of the Trust is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.
If the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same, written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained.

The Trust specifies that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.
Any additional supporting documentation for which Legal conditions is provided.

An applicable trust check does not hold or a required condition is not cleared.
Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

rule.description: Verify each stated requirement for permitted title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust, including any required Acra Senior Management exception.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
STD-7.6 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

STD-7.7 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

STD-7.8 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

ledger.clause:
4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

condition.purpose: Determine whether a DSCR below 1.0 or No Ratio transaction meets the applicable CLTV and FICO limits.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and credit_report for transaction and credit information.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether DSCR is below 1.0 or the file is No Ratio, and identify purchase, rate & term refinance, or cash-out refinance.
Validation and Verification: Compare CLTV with the applicable maximum and FICO with the minimum.
Final Determination: Record whether all applicable limits are met.
checks: For DSCR below 1.0 or No Ratio, purchase CLTV is no more than 75%.
For DSCR below 1.0 or No Ratio, refinance — rate & term CLTV is no more than 70%.
For DSCR below 1.0 or No Ratio, refinance — cash-out CLTV is no more than 65%.
For DSCR below 1.0 or No Ratio, FICO is at least 640.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable CLTV and FICO limit is met.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable CLTV or FICO limit is not met.
DSCR is not below 1.0 and the file is not No Ratio.

FICO

rule.description: Apply the stated CLTV and minimum FICO limits when DSCR is below 1.0 or the file is No Ratio.

ledger.clause:
STD-3.16 LTV \> 80.00%: requires a minimum DSCR of 1.20 and 6 months PITIA reserves; limited to SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome, PUD. Stated in LTV where the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-17. \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.17 DSCR \< 1.0 or No Ratio: maximum CLTV 75% (purchase), 70% (refinance — rate & term), 65% (refinance — cash-out); minimum FICO 640. \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.18 “The minimum rental income required is outlined in the Program Matrix.” The minimum ratios stated for particular situations across both sources are collected below; each is also stated in its own section. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

| **Situation** | **Minimum DSCR as stated** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV above 80.00% | 1.20 | S: Income Documentation |
| Loan amount over \$2,000,000 | 1.0 | S: Loan Amount |
| 1 or no score / deficient tradelines | 1.1 | S: Credit Requirements |
| Rural / unique property | 1.00 | S: Subject Property Location |
| Non-warrantable condo; condotel / PUDtel | 1.0 | S: Subject Property Type |
| First-time homebuyer | 1.150 | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property, rate & term refinance | 1.000 (“OR Maximum 40.0% DTI” — Q-14) | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property, cash-out refinance | 1.15 | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | 1.0 (“or (b) 43% maximum DTI” — Q-14) | G §11.5 |
| Mixed use, adult care or assisted living | 1.2 | G §10.7 |

STD-3.19 “File can qualify without calculating a DSCR Ratio to a maximum LTV / CLTV as described on the appropriate program matrix depending on FICO and other requirement. Requires 1007; however, DSCR is not calculated.” The Summary's No Ratio caps and minimum FICO are STD-3.17. \[G §5.33, p. 3; S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.20 “Proof of actual rents is not required. Property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies).” \[G §5.33, p. 3\]

STD-3.21 Whether No Ratio is available where another condition carries its own minimum DSCR (STD-3.16 and the table above): Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. Whether the short-term-rental caps apply to a No Ratio file: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02.

STD-3.22 Rent loss insurance applies to No Ratio DSCR (STD-8.12). \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan meets the minimum DSCR and reserve requirements stated for the applicable program scenarios.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application, appraisal_report, and credit_report for transaction, property, and credit information.
Eligibility Verification: Identify each applicable scenario listed in the checks, including any scenario requiring data not held in the case fields.
Validation and Verification: Compare DSCR with each applicable minimum and verify the stated reserves requirement when LTV is above 80.00%.
Final Determination: Record whether every applicable minimum DSCR and reserve requirement is met. Do not resolve the stated Q-14 alternatives by assumption.
checks: If LTV is above 80.00%, DSCR is at least 1.20.
If LTV is above 80.00%, reserves are at least 6 months PITIA.
If loan amount is over $2,000,000, DSCR is at least 1.0.
If there is 1 or no score / deficient tradelines, DSCR is at least 1.1.
If the property is rural / unique, DSCR is at least 1.00.
If the property is a non-warrantable condo; condotel / PUDtel, DSCR is at least 1.0.
If the borrower is a first-time homebuyer, DSCR is at least 1.150.
For a vacant property, rate & term refinance, DSCR is at least 1.000; the stated “OR Maximum 40.0% DTI” alternative is not resolved here.
For a vacant property, cash-out refinance, DSCR is at least 1.15.
If the property was listed for sale within six months, DSCR is at least 1.0; the stated “or (b) 43% maximum DTI” alternative is not resolved here.
For mixed use, adult care or assisted living, DSCR is at least 1.2.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable minimum DSCR and reserve requirement is met.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable minimum DSCR or reserve requirement is not met.
None of the listed scenarios applies to the case.

condition.purpose: Determine the DSCR for the loan using the stated formula and payment basis.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report and any lease_agreement, bank_statement, hazard_insurance, and hoa_questionnaire available for the rent and PITIA information.
Eligibility Verification: Identify annual in-place rent, market rent, and the first payment due under the Note; include subordinate financing, if applicable, in the denominator.

Validation and Verification: Calculate annual PITIA as annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees; use the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent as the numerator.
Final Determination: Divide the qualifying annual rent by annual PITIA and record the resulting DSCR. Do not resolve the stated interest-only payment question by assumption.

The denominator is the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, homeowner's / condominium association fees, and subordinate financing if applicable.
The DSCR uses the first payment due under the terms of the Note.

STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

ledger.clause:
STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions: “Minimum 700 FICO: Max 70% CLTV: DSCR ≥ 1.15: Loan amt ≤ \$1MM: NO I/O: Must Impound: Requires 6mos Reserves”. \[G §3.13, p. 10; S: Restrictions\]

STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

STD-10.3 Interest Only, 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed or 5/1 and 7/1 ARM: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.4 Interest Only, 10 Yr / 40 Year Term: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score; maximum 80% LTV / CLTV; maximum \$3M loan amount. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.5 Interest-only is not available to first-time homebuyers (STD-4.10), on vacant-property refinances (STD-8.6 and 8.7) or on properties listed for sale (STD-8.9). \[G §3.13, §10.17, §11.5\]

STD-10.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (STD-3.2; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-26). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans (first fully amortized payment on the original balance; for an ARM, the highest achievable rate at that payment's due date) is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

rule.description: Determine whether the loan qualifies by calculated DSCR or as No Ratio DSCR.

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

The Standard DSCR program finances loans on investment property, qualified on the subject property's rent rather than the borrower's income; whether every loan is a business-purpose transaction is Q-27. This section collects the program-level requirements that apply before any matrix or overlay is consulted.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required due diligence is current and covers the Key Principals and Entities identified by the guideline.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan file for borrower and guarantor due diligence and its date, and identify the entity, recourse guarantors, owners, and parties with managing control.

5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the entity file contains the required documentation without relying on borrower letters excusing or waiving any required document.
steps: Initial Document Review: Obtain and review the complete, legible formation documents and amendments; the applicable operating agreement or bylaws and amendments with referenced exhibits; ownership evidence; and the other entity documents required for this entity type and transaction.

Eligibility Verification: Confirm the operating agreement or bylaws states whether the entity is member or manager managed, authorizes borrowing money and entering into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Confirm ownership documentation identifies all persons and interests or provides compliant membership interest evidence. For corporations, review the required shareholder or stockholder certificates or stock ledger, including the required accounting of outstanding shares and any required Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate. For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, review the specified K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter.

Validation and Verification: Verify that entity-document names match identification, or review a letter of explanation addressing discrepancies; review a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent valid within ninety (90) days of closing; review any required foreign qualification; review the IRS Form SS4 or TIN or EIN issuance letter, or an EIN exception request and letter of explanation submitted for Acra Legal Department review; and review the required Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution. If a Power of Attorney is used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, review it for the stated purpose. Do not accept borrower letters stating required documents are not required, available, or excused.

Final Determination: Record whether each applicable required document and stated document content is present. Refer conflicts between formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws for additional information, and refer any additional-supporting-documentation requirement to Legal as applicable.
checks: The complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto are present.

The complete Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, with all referenced exhibits and amendments, is present and contains the required management, borrowing, mortgage-asset contract, and signer provisions.
The documentation evidencing ownership interests meets the stated requirements for the entity type.

For an S or C Corporation, the required shareholder / stockholder certificates or stock ledger is present and accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation; an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is present when required.

For an S-corporation or Partnership where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the required most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and the required CPA or Tax Preparer letter are present, including the stated alternative if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.
Names on the entity documents match the identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is present.

A Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the relevant state is present if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is conducted or the property is located.

A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.

ledger.clause:
5.2 Entity documentation
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

5.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Determine whether title may vest in the proposed inter vivos revocable trust under the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the title commitment and the complete, legible Trust or Certification of Trust, and identify the Trustors, Trustees, beneficiaries, and trust terms.

Validation and Verification: Verify that the Trust or Certification of Trust contains every stated required item. Verify the Trustee’s authority and the provisions concerning beneficiary consent, lender risk, and creditor rights. Final Determination: Record whether all applicable trust requirements are met; do not treat an irrevocable trust as permitted.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

steps: Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and, for a loan closing in the name of an entity, the entity documents and loan application for the personal guarantors and ownership information.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the file contains the history documentation required for mortgage/rental rating and DSCR payment history.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review all reported mortgages on credit and the file's documentation of mortgage and rental payment history over the last twelve (12) months.

Eligibility Verification: For DSCR loans, require documentation for the subject property, the borrower's and/or guarantor's primary residence, and second home(s), if any. Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred. For mortgages not reported on credit, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property.

Validation and Verification: Verify that the required property histories are documented and that the history can be evaluated. For a matured loan, use its maturity date for rating; verify that any extension of the maturity date is in writing.
Final Determination: Record whether the required history is documented and evaluable, and whether any applicable maturity-date extension is in writing.

ledger.clause:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Establish the DSCR using the program's stated qualifying rent, denominator, and payment basis.

The DSCR utilizes the first payment due under the terms of the Note.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-3.4 Denominator, per §5.32: “the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.5 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.6 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. The Platinum Summary does not address subordinate financing or restate the Standard Summary's HELOC calculation: Acra confirmation requested → Q-15. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.7 The program is offered through two channels with different minimum ratios: Correspondent ≥ 1.2, Wholesale ≥ 1.0 (PLAT-3.7). Matrix footnote 3 also restricts Correspondent pricing (PLAT-2.3). \[P: Minimum DSCR; matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-1.8 Every loan must meet the applicable channel minimum DSCR. The Platinum Summary lists no No Ratio option and no allowance for a ratio below 1.0; a ratio below the channel minimum does not meet the published requirement. Whether No Ratio or sub-1.0 qualification exists on this program in any form: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-1.9 Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. PLAT-1.10 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions”; the Platinum Summary refers to market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. PLAT-1.12 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-3.7 Minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio: Correspondent ≥ 1.2; Wholesale ≥ 1.0. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-3.8 Property listed for sale within six months (§11.5): the excerpt requires “≥1.0 DSCR”; on this program the channel minimum applies — Wholesale 1.0, Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11; P: Minimum DSCR\]

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.1 Occupancy: Non-Owner Occupied. \[P: Occupancy Requirements\]

PLAT-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” The property types the Platinum Summary lists as eligible are at PLAT-7.1; types it does not list are set out in the table at 7.1 and asked in Q-07. \[G §3.41, p. 11; P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR Platinum” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (PLAT-8.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

PLAT-1.4 Eligible loan purpose types: Purchase, Rate & Term Refinance, Cash-Out Refinance, Delayed Financing. The matrix footnote states “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”; which matrix column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements; matrix footnote\]

PLAT-1.5 “Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) Cash-Out Refinance Transactions requires current lease agreement”. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-1.6 “Vacant properties ineligible”. The Seller's Guide provisions on vacant purchases and §10.17 vacant refinances therefore do not apply (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

rule.description: Determine whether the subject property meets the program’s non-owner-occupied requirement.

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.1 Occupancy: Non-Owner Occupied. \[P: Occupancy Requirements\]

PLAT-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” The property types the Platinum Summary lists as eligible are at PLAT-7.1; types it does not list are set out in the table at 7.1 and asked in Q-07. \[G §3.41, p. 11; P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR Platinum” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (PLAT-8.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

PLAT-1.4 Eligible loan purpose types: Purchase, Rate & Term Refinance, Cash-Out Refinance, Delayed Financing. The matrix footnote states “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”; which matrix column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements; matrix footnote\]

PLAT-1.5 “Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) Cash-Out Refinance Transactions requires current lease agreement”. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-1.6 “Vacant properties ineligible”. The Seller's Guide provisions on vacant purchases and §10.17 vacant refinances therefore do not apply (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

Platinum Select finances loans on non-owner occupied property, qualified on the subject property's rent, within a narrower box than the Standard program; whether every loan is a business-purpose transaction is Q-22. This section collects the program-level requirements that apply before the matrix or any condition is consulted.

| **Question and Acra's source language** | **Confirmation requested** | **Acra response or correction** |

| Q-01 The 721 threshold and Correspondent limits (PLAT-2.1 to 2.3). Matrix rows: 730 / 721 / 700; footnote 3: “Correspondent Pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 FICO”; ARM margin bands 720-759 and 700-719. | \(a\) Is the 721 threshold intended, or should it read 720? (b) For a score of exactly 720: which matrix row, is it subject to the Correspondent 60% limit, and which ARM margin? (c) For Correspondent loans at 700-719, does the 60% limit apply to purchase and rate & term while the matrix's 55% governs cash-out? |  |
| Q-02 Delayed financing (PLAT-1.4, 2.4). Listed as an eligible loan purpose; footnote: “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. | Which matrix column governs delayed financing, and which cash-in-hand rule applies? |  |
| Q-03 Qualifying rent (PLAT-3.1, 3.2). Platinum: “the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent … 2 months’ proof of receipts … lease … in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing”. §5.32: “the lesser of …”; “two (2) consecutive months”; “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” | \(a\) Does the Platinum greater-of rule govern this program in place of the §5.32 formula? (b) Must the 2 months of receipts be consecutive? (c) Do the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply? (d) Is any additional approval required to use actual rent? |  |

| §7.4 Debt Ratio Calculation; DTI portion of §7.5; §11.5 43% DTI alternative | §7.3: no DTI is calculated for DSCR-qualified applicants | Not restated; asked (Q-14) |
